title: What survives the copy?
hook: Predict the result, then reveal the sequence.

knows: DNA and RNA are sequences of chemical building blocks.
doesNotKnow: The two original strands separate and each acts as a template. Each resulting double helix contains one original strand and one newly synthesised complementary strand.

misconception: The original sequence and the resulting sequence must have the same interpretation.
objective: The two original strands separate and each acts as a template. Each resulting double helix contains one original strand and one newly synthesised complementary strand.

claims.text: Question, answer, diagram and explanation: During semiconservative DNA replication, what does each newly formed double helix contain? The two original strands separate and each acts as a template. Each resulting double helix contains one original strand and one newly synthesised complementary strand.
Recall: How many original strands does each daughter double helix contain after semiconservative copying? Each daughter double helix contains one old strand and one newly synthesised strand.
The figure is a simplified model and is not to scale.

recall.question: How many original strands does each daughter double helix contain after semiconservative copying?
recall.why: Each daughter double helix contains one old strand and one newly synthesised strand.
